problem_text:
A manufacturing network aims to devise a strategy for lowering total energy waste from several production facilities. Presently, no conservation measures are in place.

The operational profile for each facility is as follows:
* For Plant A, energy intensity is 2.395, output volume is 73.263.
* For Plant B, energy intensity is 2.227, output volume is 105.399.
* For Plant C, energy intensity is 2.115, output volume is 222.947.
* For Plant D, energy intensity is 1.727, output volume is 126.552.
* For Plant E, energy intensity is 2.482, output volume is 195.389.

To curtail waste, several conservation technologies can be implemented, each with a distinct efficiency in reducing energy loss:
* Technology 1 reduces waste by 52%
* Technology 2 reduces waste by 48%
* Technology 3 reduces waste by 56%
* Technology 4 reduces waste by 30%
* Technology 5 reduces waste by 64%

Deploying a technology at a facility entails an incremental cost per unit of output. The cost matrix for all facility-technology pairings is provided below:

| Facility \ Technology | Tech1 | Tech2 | Tech3 | Tech4 | Tech5 |
|--|-|-|-|-|
| Plant A | 143.542 | 61.474 | 57.767 | 32.925 | 46.591 |
| Plant B | 32.715 | 111.814 | 154.816 | 45.178 | 51.113 |
| Plant C | 101.998 | 147.671 | 195.555 | 109.681 | 63.77 |
| Plant D | 29.1 | 46.882 | 53.222 | 44.094 | 12.688 |
| Plant E | 111.486 | 62.119 | 195.116 | 115.138 | 142.509 |

The network must decide which technologies to apply at each facility (facilities may employ multiple technologies concurrently), and a facility may also operate with partial conservation if needed.
The objective is to guarantee that the aggregate energy waste is diminished by at least a fraction P = 0.263 of the baseline amount, while minimizing the overall expenditure.
